title: Implement Adversarial Robustness Evaluation Pipeline
description: The ChromaticCanvas Trainer project currently trains and serves a model for an image-related task. To improve the model's reliability, we need to add a feature to evaluate its robustness against adversarial attacks. This task involves implementing an evaluation pipeline using a common and simple attack method, the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM). The implementation will span multiple files and require careful integration with the existing training, configuration, and serving infrastructure. This task is designed to be completed over multiple development sessions, testing the agent's ability to retain context and build upon previous work.

project_spec.name: ChromaticCanvas Trainer
project_spec.description:
ChromaticCanvas Trainer is a lightweight C-based machine-learning training suite that helps digital artists and creative coders build, tweak, and serve models that predict harmonious color palettes from sketches or mood-board keywords. Centered around an MVC design, the project splits data handling (Model), user/visualization logic (View), and training/serving control flow (Controller) to keep creative experimentation fast and modular.

Within the pipeline, artists drag-and-drop reference images or keyword lists into the View layer; the Controller orchestrates a data_preprocessing stage that extracts color histograms and semantic embeddings, stores features in an on-disk SQLite feature_store, and kicks off tiny feed-forward networks whose hyperparameter_tuning is driven by simple grid search. experiment_tracking logs every trial to a lightweight JSON registry, while the Observer_Pattern pushes live metrics to an SDL window so designers can watch loss curves evolve like abstract art. Once a satisfactory palette model emerges, the Model_Registry registers the binary in a versioned directory, enabling immediate model_serving through a REST endpoint. model_monitoring then streams real-time predictions and drift statistics, alerting creatives if their color trends go out of fashion.

Though scoped for easy complexity, ChromaticCanvas Trainer delivers a full creative ML loop in just 15 concise files, making it an ideal starter project for those who want to explore artistic machine learning without leaving the comfort of plain ANSI C.
dependencies: GNU Scientific Library – GSL (numerical routines for training)
